subject: Calendar and capacity
question: Which calendar dates define the week, what is the presentation deadline, and what hours can each person commit?
safe_behavior: Use Day 1 to Day 7 only; do not invent dates or hours.

subject: Demonstration boundaries
question: For each strategy part, approve the working feature, synthetic input and explicitly mocked integration. Must OCR, biometrics, USSD, WhatsApp, preauthorization creation and anomaly scoring work this week?
safe_behavior: Five dimensions remain required. Do not silently omit a dimension or call a mock live.
answer: Lameck approved the health claims-and-rules frontend slice on 2026-10-10: synthetic data; structured preauthorization request/review; no OCR, AI/anomaly scoring, biometrics, WhatsApp or USSD; member history/consent deferred from this slice. This records frontend scope only; broader five-part demonstration boundaries remain open.

subject: Technical conventions and API freeze
proposed_coordinators: Tristan/Brian and Obunde with frontend owners
question: Approve modular FastAPI architecture, ORM and migrations, package versions, API paths, response schemas, money representation and repository layout. Is the proposed SRS contract accepted or amended?
blocks: Shared schema, framework setup, clients and implementation contract
safe_behavior: Next.js, TypeScript, FastAPI and PostgreSQL are confirmed; other libraries and protocol details are proposed.
answer: Lameck approved on 2026-10-10 using proposed REST/OpenAPI v0.1 as the frontend integration direction and extending it for policy/rule catalogue and version-history operations. UI must represent unavailable APIs honestly. Frontend scaffold uses Next.js App Router/TypeScript with Next 16.4.0 and React 19.3.0 generated by create-next-app; Node.js >=20.9.0 is required. Shared error/nullable semantics and final cross-team API freeze remain open. | Obunde decided on 2026-10-10 (T04 brief; recorded 2026-10-13): Python 3.12; PostgreSQL 16; plain pinned requirements.txt; SQLAlchemy 2.x async with asyncpg; Alembic configured for async; one migration history shared by all backend developers; module layers models.py, dtos.py, services.py, controllers.py (controllers hold the router); GET /health; everything runs via Docker Compose. Still open: schema per module vs default (Tristan/Brian), API contract and error envelope (T03), money column details beyond integer minor units plus currency. See DECISION_LOG.md.

subject: Identity and access
question: Keycloak is selected for identity and Auth.js for the frontend OIDC/session integration. Confirm final role grants, organization membership and consent ownership, and implement server-side API token and tenant-scope enforcement.
blocks: Login, authorization, API data filtering and consent ownership
safe_behavior: A role picker is not authentication. Do not issue insecure demo bypasses as live access control.
answer: Lameck approved on 2026-10-10: provider billers submit claims and respond to requests; insurer/TPA reviewers assess and request corrections; only explicitly authorized users approve; insurer finance records payments and reconciles, without changing adjudication. TPA rule publication is prohibited unless the insurer explicitly delegates that permission. Keycloak is the selected identity provider and Auth.js handles the Next.js OpenID Connect authorization-code + PKCE session. Exact tenant/organization grant model, backend token verification, consent ownership and production deployment remain open. | Obunde answered on 2026-10-12 after a conflict with the T06 brief (backend email/password JWTs, 5 roles): use Keycloak as the identity provider and Lameck's 10 Keycloak realm roles as the application roles; the backend verifies Keycloak-signed access tokens and does not issue tokens or store passwords. Still open: permission grants per role, mapping of Keycloak tenant_ids/organization_ids to backend records, patient role, consent ownership, TPA read access to payments/reports, production deployment. See DECISION_LOG.md 2026-10-12. Follow-up (Obunde, 2026-10-12): roles from the Keycloak token, permissions per role in Postgres; Keycloak role/user revocation applies at token expiry; grant table recorded in DECISION_LOG.md 2026-10-12; patient kept as an 11th Keycloak role; tpa-reviewer gets no reports:read or payments:read; history:read and consent:manage granted to no role while D07 is deferred.
approved_by: Lameck (role boundaries and Keycloak selection; server-side enforcement remains open); Obunde (Keycloak + Lameck's 10 roles for the backend, conflict resolution)

subject: Financial policy and exceptions
question: Outside Case 001, confirm deductible and coinsurance order, benefit consumption basis, reservation timing, exclusions, rounding, partial approval, reversals and who absorbs each adjustment.

Detailed general financial calculation/accounting rules remain open.

subject: Policy and rule governance
proposed_coordinators: Insurer product/benefits owner with compliance and access-control owner; Silas records
question: Name the accountable insurer business owner and rule-drafter roles, and define the scope and controls for any insurer-to-TPA publication delegation.
blocks: Live rule authoring, approval, publication and delegated TPA permissions
safe_behavior: An independent insurer-authorized approver is mandatory for publication; the approver must be distinct from the rule author. A TPA cannot publish insurer rules unless the insurer explicitly grants scoped permission. The UI may show the workflow but cannot grant permissions.
answer: Lameck approved on 2026-10-10 that every policy/rule publication requires an independent insurer-authorized approver distinct from the author. TPA users may publish only under explicit, scoped insurer delegation. Accountable insurer business-owner and drafter job titles, delegation scope detail, and any additional compliance sign-off remain open.
